Elena — attaching the technical protocol draft and a sample regression matrix for your review (redwood-eval-protocol-v1.pdf, sample-regression-matrix.csv). Highlights below.

Summary (technical highlights):
- NIST mapping: we map "Map" => Model inventory & lineage (artifact hashes, training/finetune metadata), "Measure" => model evaluation suites (unit tests, held-out clinical eval sets, fairness checks), "Manage" => CI/CD policies for model rollouts and canary thresholds, "Govern" => policy & role mapping in Console with audit trails. The one-pager will have explicit control IDs and evidence artifacts (audit logs, model manifests, eval reports).

- EU AI Act classification: For Palisade's described use (triage/decision-support with potential safety impact), a hosted Redwood endpoint used directly in clinical workflow would likely be assessed as high-risk. Redwood's hosted product provides technical mitigations (explainability artifacts, logging, version pinning, human override hooks), but Palisade must own risk acceptance, clinical validation, and operational deployment controls (consent, clinical oversight). Our mapping separates obligations by design/deployment.

- Eval & Regression protocol:
  * Pre-release: For each major model version we recommend stratified sampling across clinical intents. Minimum acceptance sample: 1,000 de-identified cases (when available) or a statistically equivalent synthetic/benchmarked set when PHI cannot be shared. For lower-volume intents, use focused scenario-driven suites (n>200).
  * Metrics: clinical precision/recall (task-specific), calibration (Brier/Expected Calibration Error), hallucination rate (measured with a curated ground-truth set), safety-critical false-positive/negative rates, and a risk-weighted utility score.
  * Regression detection: baseline vs candidate comparison with bootstrap confidence intervals; absolute metric delta thresholds + percent-change rules. We recommend automated gating: any metric drop >3% absolute or >10% relative triggers hold and an engineer/clinical reviewer triage.
  * Continuous monitoring: token-level telemetry, sampling of live outputs (weekly), drift detection (embedding-level drift with KL/Population Stability Index), and monthly summaries.

- Tooling: Redwood Optimize integrates lightweight evaluation hooks to run suites on dedicated capacity and stores historical eval runs in the Console for rollbacks/forensic analysis.

Open items we still want to confirm for Palisade: preferred acceptance thresholds per intent, availability of de-identified test sets, and whether you require sample-level provenance for every evaluation artifact.

Thanks — happy to present these in Thursday's sync.

— Priyom
Principal Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
